sections.h2: Shade or sun: the lot shapes the plan
body: Two Fort White homes of the same size can need very different jobs. A riverfront house under tree canopy near Ichetucknee stays damp. Mildew grows on the siding, soffits hold moisture, and the bottom row of boards takes splash-back with every storm. A ranch house on open land bakes all day, so color fades, caulk dries out and cracks, and wood trim checks. Residential painting in Fort White, FL starts by figuring out which situation you are in, and the prep plan follows from that.

Shaded homes get a thorough mildew treatment and wash, then time to dry before primer. The crew lead takes moisture readings on suspect siding and trim. Anything soft gets replaced rather than painted over. Our article on hidden siding moisture damage explains why moisture you can't see causes so many paint failures.

Sun-exposed houses need fresh, flexible sealant at every seam and a 100% acrylic topcoat that holds color under strong UV. Dramatic color changes get a third coat. On long, unshaded elevations, crews work around the sun and avoid spraying a wall while it is hot enough to flash-dry the paint. Porch floors, railings, and front doors get tougher enamels. If you are rethinking the color scheme, a Fort White color consultation can help, and colors can be matched from a chip or a leftover can.

Interiors get the same care. Crews move and protect furniture, patch and spot-prime walls, and work one room at a time, so you don't need to leave. A single room usually takes one day, and a whole interior takes three days to two weeks. See our interior painting in Fort White page for room-by-room details.
bullets: Exterior: wash, scrape, repair, caulk, prime, two coats
Interior: patch, sand, cut in, two coats

body: Each project ends with a punch walk you sign. Anything that isn't right gets fixed before the job is closed. Exteriors carry a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years, in addition to the manufacturer's warranty. For the wider picture, see our residential painting page or return to the Fort White hub.

faqs.q: Can you paint my Fort White home while I live in it?
faqs.a: Yes. We move and protect furniture and work room by room. You don't need to leave.

faqs.q: Why does my riverfront house mildew so quickly after painting?
faqs.a: Shade and damp air keep the walls wet. Killing growth at the root, letting the surface dry, and checking moisture before priming are what make a repaint last.

faqs.q: How long does an exterior repaint take?
faqs.a: Usually three to seven working days, plus time for washing and drying. Your estimate includes the schedule.

faqs.q: Can you replace soft trim on my house before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Rot, trim, and fascia replacement are part of prep. Each repair is photographed and listed on the estimate so you know what is being fixed and why.
